Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be an operator to assist you. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; and David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: expanding operating margins through scale and efficiency, improving gross margins with technical optimizations and product mix shifts, delivering robust net revenue retention fueled by expansions, maintaining disciplined operating expense management across R&D, sales and marketing, and G&A, and growing average contract values via land-and-expand motions.

These efforts highlight the operating leverage in our SaaS model as we scale CloudForge Enterprise, our comprehensive AI-powered cloud data orchestration solution serving over 2,500 customers, including Fortune 500 leaders like Procter & Gamble and Salesforce. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $285 million, representing a 38% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.4%, and non-GAAP operating income was $63.6 million, delivering a 22.3% operating margin.

Turning first to our gross margin performance, which continues to reflect the scalability and efficiency inherent in our SaaS model. For Q2 FY2024, we delivered a GAAP gross margin of 82.4%, up 180 basis points year-over-year from the prior period and building on sequential gains. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based compensation and amortization of acquired intangibles, it expanded to around 83.8%, showing continued improvement.

This robust expansion underscores several key drivers aligned with CloudForge's evolution as a leader in AI-powered enterprise workflow automation, blending collaboration depth with automation prowess optimized for mid-market and enterprise scalability. Scale efficiencies form the bedrock here. While cost of revenues grew more slowly than revenue, hosting and bandwidth—comprising the bulk of COGS—benefited from higher utilization of our multi-tenant architecture. As new Fortune 500 wins in financial services ramped seat counts and module adoption, we spread costs across a broader base without proportional capacity investments.

Sequentially, technical optimizations played a big role. We've accelerated migration to next-gen ARM-based instances like AWS Graviton3 processors, delivering 40% better price-performance than x86 equivalents, reducing effective hosting costs per TB of data processed by 22% quarter-over-quarter. Our proprietary data compression algorithms in CloudForge AI, now live in 70% of deployments, cut storage egress fees by 15%, even as we handle 2.5x more AI inference workloads without ballooning bandwidth expenses.

Year-over-year, product mix shifts drove much of the lift. Subscription revenue from high-margin AI modules like our Autonomous Workflow Engine and Predictive Analytics add-ons now makes up a larger share of total ARR, up significantly from last year, versus lower-margin legacy conversions. These AI tiers command over 90% gross margins, pulling the blended rate higher. We also held firm on pricing discipline, implementing modest list price increases on enterprise tiers with minimal pushback, supported by our strong net retention.

Regionally, North America, our largest market at 85% of revenue, held high margins around 84%, aided by mature self-serve onboarding that trims professional services costs. EMEA, now 10% of revenue after solid growth, operates around 79% despite initial localization investments, thanks to new data sovereignty zones. APAC at 5% improved as we localized edge caching for latency-sensitive workloads. These trends position us for our long-term 85% non-GAAP gross margin target, with investments in zero-touch provisioning and serverless AI inference, partnering with NVIDIA for GPU gains that could further reduce COGS as gen-AI surges. Early pilots are showing 30% fewer support tickets via AI diagnostics.

That said, we're watchful for hyperscaler pricing volatility and upticks in support for complex AI customizations, but our strong balance sheet gives us flexibility.

Building on this, let's look at our overall operating performance. I'm pleased to report that our non-GAAP operating margin for Q2 came in at 22.3%, up 450 basis points year-over-year and 210 basis points sequentially. This marks our seventh straight quarter of expansion, with trailing twelve-month non-GAAP operating margin at 21.8%. On a GAAP basis, it was 18.7%, accounting for stock-based compensation and amortization from recent acquisitions.

The key drivers highlight the operating leverage in our SaaS model. Revenue scale and mix shift provided the primary tailwind. Our $285 million top line, driven by 125% net revenue retention from upsells in the AI Data Pipeline module, gave significant fixed-cost leverage. Large enterprise deals, averaging $1.2 million in total contract value, now represent 55% of bookings, up from 45% a year ago. This cohort shows dollar-based net expansion of 132%, with consumption-based pricing on GPU-accelerated workloads growing 55% year-over-year, outpacing seat-based legacy SKUs.

Sales and marketing efficiency added another tailwind. S&M expenses fell to 28% of revenue from 32% last year, with payback periods compressing to 14 months from 18. Customer acquisition cost ratio improved to 0.85x on a last twelve months basis, thanks to product-led growth. We expanded freemium tiers for CloudForge Developer Studio, driving 40% of new ARR from self-serve, and targeted account-based marketing in financial services and healthcare boosted win rates to 45%, with marketing efficiency at a magic number of 1.4x.

R&D optimization was neutral to a slight headwind. Spend held at 18% of revenue, with 60% now in AI/ML, including the AutoScale Engine for dynamic data ingestion costs on AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI. This reduced engineering churn below 10% and launched 12 major updates. ROI is showing in NRR uplift of about 200 basis points.

Cost of revenue discipline, as I detailed earlier, contributed positively through hyperscaler renegotiations shaving 15% off hosting costs per TB and multi-tenant efficiencies cutting support tickets 25%.

Regionally, North America drove 40% ARR growth with 25% margins, EMEA bookings up 60% post-GDPR features building to 20% margins, and APAC 80% growth despite higher infra costs. Macro headwinds eased, pushing our Rule of 40 score to 62, well above peers.

This profile sets us up for 25-27% long-term non-GAAP operating margins by FY2026 at 30%+ ARR growth, with levers like AI monetization, land-and-expand targeting 130% NRR, and M&A synergies from our Q1 DataSync AI acquisition delivering 300 basis points in costs.

Now, drilling into operating expenses, which totaled around $171 million, up modestly year-over-year but reflecting leverage as they came in below revenue growth pace, now at 79% of revenue down from higher prior levels. This supports our Rule of 40 path.

R&D expenses were $42 million, up 18% year-over-year at 22% of revenue, our largest area to maintain product leadership in enterprise collaboration SaaS. The increase funded a 15% headcount ramp to 850 engineers on the AI-native roadmap, including ForgeAI Assistant, our generative AI copilot for devops and teams, driving 35% higher feature adoption in top customers. 60% US-based in San Francisco and Austin, 25% in Bangalore for model training efficiencies, with cloud compute costs down 10%. We'll hold R&D at 20-22% through FY2025 for zero-trust security and multimodal AI, fueling 118% NRR.

Sales and marketing at $52 million, up 10% year-over-year at 32% of revenue. Growth moderated on tough comps, driven by commissions on $45 million new ACV up 32%, including a $12 million Fortune 50 deal. CAC down 8% to $4,200 per ARR dollar via PLG freemium converting at 22%, ABM in healthcare and manufacturing. 40% digital marketing ROI 4.5x, events 15% of pipeline. US 70% bookings, EMEA 45% growth, APAC accelerating. Sales productivity up 22% with AI lead scoring, payback 14 months, targeting 125% NRR amid macro caution.

G&A at $34 million, up 4% at 21% of revenue. SBC down to 7% of revenue post-IPO normalization, headcount up 3% for compliance. Professional fees down 12% via AI tools, facilities savings $2 million from remote work. Fell from 24% YoY, expect 18-20% forward with ESG and cyber investments.

Overall, this demonstrates discipline: innovation in R&D, efficient growth in S&M, scaling G&A.

Shifting to net revenue retention, a cornerstone of our flywheel. For Q2, NRR was 122%, up 300 basis points sequentially and from last year, at the high end of peers amid macro pressures on SMB budgets.

Expansion added 28 points, from upsells and usage. Upsell velocity up 15%, with 42% of top 500 adopting ForgeAI Pro for workflow automation, adding 35% ARR. Cross-sells in security for fintech/healthcare, usage in analytics +12 points from petabyte ramps.

Contraction -6 points, better than expected via customer success ML signals preempting downsells. Enterprise negligible.

Churn -4 points, logo 3.2% annualized enterprise vs. 7% SMB. Retained 95% at-risk via TAMs with AI health scores, pruning non-strategic retail.

North America 122% with hyperscaler billing, EMEA 115% DACH strong, APAC 108% countered by Singapore hub.

Our platform-of-platforms, zero-ETL, API extensibility drive 130% NRR target by FY25, enterprise focus 65% expansions.

Finally, average contract value came in at $178,000, up 12% sequentially and 22% year-over-year, TTM $172,000 up 18%, fifth straight double-digit quarter.

NRR upsells drove it, whale accounts +35% with ForgeAI bundling, from $120k to $250k. New customer ACV record $192k up 28%, upmarket to Fortune 1000, like $3.2M European OEM IoT.

North America $195k 68% bookings, EMEA $162k, APAC $138k up 40%. Platformization, Elite bundles 42%, displacing legacy 22% deals 1.8x ACV. Q3 $180-185k expected.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $1.2 billion, providing flexibility for strategic acquisitions and growth.

We're updating full-year guidance: revenue $1.15 billion to $1.20 billion, reflecting first-half strength.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa for a technology update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress advancing our AI capabilities and integrating them into our core platform. We're seeing strong adoption of ForgeAI-powered features, driving higher user engagement and better customer outcomes. We've also enhanced platform security and scalability to meet enterprise demands, including zero-ETL pipelines and edge inference.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

David Kim:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative, contributing about 25% to our Q2 revenue growth through rapid upsells and new logos. It's landing in 65% of new customers and expanding in 42% of our top enterprise accounts, directly boosting NRR by 10-15 points in those cohorts. Attach rates are strong at 60-70% in multi-year deals, especially bundled with data pipeline and analytics modules, mirroring how peers have scaled AI add-ons. Early usage data shows 2x inference workloads, and we're pricing premium tiers to capture that value while keeping payback efficient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Emily. International is a key growth driver, and APAC is early innings but accelerating at 80% year-over-year. We've launched a Singapore hub and Tokyo data center, tailoring integrations for Tencent and Alibaba Cloud, targeting banks and manufacturing. Bookings up sharply, ACV jumping 40%, though higher infra costs initially. We'll invest in local sales teams and resellers like NTT, aiming for 15% of revenue by FY2025, offsetting U.S.-China tensions with diversification. EMEA similarly ramping post-GDPR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Mike Patel:
Great question, Raj. Churn remains low and manageable at 3.2% annualized for enterprise, 7% SMB, flat sequentially. We're proactive with Customer Success 2.0, using ML-driven health scores and dedicated TAMs to retain 95% of at-risk cohorts—preempting contractions via expansion playbooks. Economic pressures hit SMB pricing a bit, but enterprise multi-year autos hold firm.

NRR trending up to 122% this quarter, +300 bps sequential, led by 28-point expansions from ForgeAI upsells (42% adoption, 35% ARR add) and usage growth. Contractions -6 points offset by interventions, churn -4 points. North America 122%, EMEA 115%, APAC 108%. This resilience supports our 130% target, even as peers see higher SMB churn.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
